controls: Environmental permit monitoring is being planned
Record and follow the measurement methodology required by the permit.
Environmental permit monitoring is being planned
Use the monitoring frequency specified by the permit.
Environmental permit monitoring results are produced
Follow the reporting procedure specified by the permit.
Compliant measurements reported in a non-compliant way
A stack-emission method must be selected
Use standards from recognised standards-making organisations wherever possible.
A monitoring organisation performs stack-emission testing
Require an EN ISO/IEC 17025 quality system.
Monitoring without a laboratory quality framework
A monitoring organisation performs stack-emission testing
Require demonstrated technical competence under EN ISO/IEC 17025.
Require evidence that the laboratory can generate technically valid results.
Manual stack monitoring is carried out
A standard has an Environment Agency MID
Apply the relevant Method Implementation Document consistently.
Inconsistent implementation of the same standard
Carry out the required risk assessment.
Use a site-specific protocol / measurement plan.
Use the standard MCERTS reporting format.
Manual stack samples require laboratory analysis
Use a laboratory accredited to the MCERTS performance standard for stack-emission samples.
Measurements are taken at discrete intervals
Treat them as periodic measurements rather than continuous monitoring.
A manual periodic technique is used
Extract the sample on site and analyse it using the applicable laboratory method.
Calling a non-manual route manual sampling
A transportable automated instrument is used periodically
Treat it as on-site periodic instrumental monitoring.
Misclassifying portable instrumental monitoring as permanent CEMS
A small stack-gas sample represents the emission stream
Require the collected material to represent the overall character of the stack gas.
Non-representative sample used as the emission result
Use fewer samples only when the gas is sufficiently homogeneous; increase sampling when heterogeneous.
A monitoring uncertainty budget is considered
Treat sampling uncertainty as potentially larger than analytical uncertainty and control sampling accordingly.
Use isokinetic sampling to obtain a representative particle-size distribution.
Calculate the required sampling flow from nozzle area and gas velocity.
Nozzle and stack velocities are available
Calculate nozzle velocity divided by stack-gas velocity and express as a percentage.
Required and actual sampling flow rates are available
Cross-check actual flow divided by required flow during monitoring.
Drift from isokinetic sampling going undetected
Mean actual isokinetic ratio is evaluated for EN 13284-1 dust sampling
Reject the measurement when the mean ratio is outside -5% to +15% of the required value.
Sampling velocity is below the isokinetic target
Flag potential bias toward larger particles and possible concentration overestimation.
Sampling velocity is above the isokinetic target
Flag potential bias toward smaller particles and possible concentration underestimation.
An extracted sample is conditioned before analysis
Ensure conditioning does not alter the substance being monitored.
Particulate carry-over could affect an extractive gas measurement
Use an appropriate probe filter where required.
Condensation could occur during sample transport
Use a heated sample line where required to prevent condensation.
Loss of soluble or condensable analyte
Moisture must be removed before analysis
Use a suitable cooling system or permeation dryer without altering the measurand.
Water interference or uncontrolled sample loss
Dynamic dilution is used for sample conditioning
Apply a known dilution factor sufficient to keep the sample below its dew point.
